From the results obtained, it can be observed that this coefficient of determination improves in cases where TDA is used as a pipeline to machine learning schemes. These results underline the significance of the approach reported in this paper.

articleTitle: The Application of IoT-Controlled Electrical Device by Using Smartphone Speech Recognition among People with Mobility Impairment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This article aims to present a method for controlling electrical devices by means of speech recognition technology that can be used through smartphones. In order to make the system more efficient, it is designed to run on an Internet of Things or IoT base which providing an option to facilitate use for people with mobility impairment. Working system in this research has been divided into three parts; part 1) the low-power control circuit which serves to control and monitor the operating status of the electrical devices, part 2) the Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) server of IoT on signal and message transport protocol and message queuing, and part 3) smart mobile applications or smartphones which accept voice commands by using speech recognition or speech-to-text methods to control the device part 1) through MQTT server of IoT in part 2), where these 3 parts will work together interactively. The results of the speech control experiment showed transcription accuracy by type of on and off commands was 99.36 percent of office environments and quiet streets and 98.00 percent of busy and chaotic traffic environments. Also, it showed 98.21 percent of people with mobility impairment can actually use it.

articleTitle: OCR Error Correction Using BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Language models have critical importance in the pre- and post-processing of optical character recognition (OCR). The quality of documents and scanners is important for OCR systems, with inferior quality leading to more erroneous output. For long time intervals of sequences, long short-term memory (LSTM) fulfills the requirements because it can solve problems with long-term dependencies. In this study, we evaluate the performance of error correction for OCR data using LSTM. The results show that we have good performance for correcting error words by using bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM). We obtain 98.13% better performance in correcting error words by using OCRd data and 97.18% better performance by using social media data. In this respect, we show that the method we have applied can be used for error corrections.

articleTitle: Pinned Buried PIN Photodiode Type Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper reviews the origin of Pinned Buried Photodiode and its historical development efforts. Three original Japanese Patent Applications filed by Hagiwara at Sony in 1975 are explained in details which defined the first triple junction type Pinned Buried Photo diode with the in-pixel vertical overflow drain (VOD) function with the electrical shutter capability, realizing the completely film-free and mechanical-parts-free all-digital solid-state image sensors. It is shown that the conventional PN junction depletion region is not the only place to have a barrier potential needed for photo electron hole pair separation. A clever doping-engineering of the pinned surface P+ P hole accumulation region can also create the surface barrier electric field to enhance drastically the photo electron and hole pair separations to increase the short-wave blue light sensitivity. It is concluded that this surface P+P doping-engineering possibly creates Pinned Buried PIN Photo diode Type Solar Cell with a better quantum efficiency.

articleTitle: Isolated Handwritten Pashto Characters Recognition using KNN classifier
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Regional and cultural diversities around the world and especially in Pakistan has given birth to a large number of writing systems and scripts consists of varying character sets. Developing an optimal OCR system for such a varying and large character set is a challenging task. Unlimited variations in handwritten texts due to mood swings, varying writing styles, changes in medium of writing, etc. puzzles the research community. Slight change in character shapes for various scripts acts as a big barrier in developing the character recognition (CR) systems for cursive scripts. Unavailability of benchmark results and corpora for cursive scripts CR impedes the researchers in the development of an optimal CR systems. To efficiently address these issues, the proposed research work aims to develop an optimum OCR system for the recognition of handwritten Pashto characters. Also the unavailability of a standard corpora of the handwritten Pashto characters is addressed by developing a medium sized corpus of the handwritten Pashto characters (14784 handwritten samples). K nearest neighbor is adapted for the recognition of the Pashto characters based on the zoning technique. After testing the proposed OCR system for varying training and test sets an overall accuracy of 85.31% is calculated.

articleTitle: Power Transformer Design Implementation for Large-Scale Solar Power Plant Grid Integration
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: South Africa is currently facing shortage of electricity, as the national utility is forced to implement routine load shedding stages. To tackle this problem, the country has planned to boost its electricity infrastructure through the systematic development of renewable energy independent power projects to provide additional capacity for the national grid. In this study, the design of a 60 MVA 88/33 kV YNd1 power transformer is implemented for a solar photovoltaic (PV) plant. The power transformer is designed and tested at SGB-SMIT POWER MATLA. The transformer is designed using an in-house transformer design system (TDS) to predict the performance. The transformer is then manufactured, tested and successfully installed on site. The factory acceptance tests (FAT) on thermal and short-circuit, as well as conducted no-load, load and short-circuit impedance tests confirmed the transformer specifications and suitability for the proposed project. The specified impedance is 11 % which is the same as the measured impedance, the former is over by 0.2 % to cater for internal production tolerances that have been experienced over the years.

articleTitle: Robust Spectrum Sensing Scheme against Malicious Users Attack in a Cognitive Radio Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) scheme for detection of primary user (PU) in a cognitive radio network. Our scheme is based on a separating-hyperplane that discriminates between ellipsoids corresponding to two hypotheses. Additionally, we present a method to eliminate malicious cognitive radio users (MCRUs) that send false sensing data to the fusion center (FC) and degrade the system's detection performance. Simulation results verify the outperformance of the proposed method for the elimination of MCRUs and detection of PU.

articleTitle: Organic Thin-Films by Wet-Processes for Flexible Bulk-Heterojunction Organic Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this work, poly(3, 4-ethylenedioxythiophene) blended to polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) and poly(3-hexylthiophene) composite with 1-(3-methoxycarbonyl)propyl-1-phenyl[6], [6]C61 (P3HT: PCBM) deposited by spin and blade coating were thoroughly investigated by optical, morphological, and structural characterization techniques targeting the improvement of organic solar cells (OSCs). Processing parameters as surface treatment, filtration, concentration, additives, and deposition speed were studied in order to optimize OSC performance. The hole transport layer by spin coating featured a thickness of ca. 50 nm, a roughness of 2 nm, and absorbance lower than 0.03. Deposition by blade coating reduced film thickness and roughness to approx. 20 nm and 1.5 nm, respectively. It also brought further down thin-film absorption in the visible spectrum. P3HT: PCBM thickness could be easily varied from 100 to 200 nm by both deposition techniques. Absorbance (maximum of 0.4) and XRD data demonstrated enhanced thin-film crystallinity for P3HT: PCBM spun from 26 mg/mL solutions. Semiconducting films by blade coating provided thicker films <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${(> 140\ \text{nm})}$</tex> and an even higher absorption (0.5 - 0.8) due to the p-type molecule. The next step is to integrate these films to flexible OSCs.

articleTitle: Fractal Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This work is aimed to gain artificial neural network architecture that allows to recognize such events in video stream data that merit higher attention. The convolutional neural networks, being used commonly in image recognition, are rather inappropriate for those purposes due to their slowness and poor re-training abilities for real-time systems. Other known architectures suffer from overfitting while re-training. This paper contains some new ideas that proposed to be solution for the several problems at once. The self-similarity allows to replicate the training process. The network is not fully connected that leads to the possibility to consider partial training procedures (explained in text). The training procedure does not use gradient descents, but built using fast and precise linear algebra methods (although the nonlinearity preserved in activation functions). Finally, there is special property that allows the proposed network to be suitable for video first of all: when the frames have small difference between them, the recognition and even re-training are fast due to just channels with changed signals are in use. The first experiments confirm the efficiency of the architecture for the simple video streams.

articleTitle: Sources of Electric Power to Meet Demand and Reduce Carbon Footprint at an Urban University Campus
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Regulatory bodies are setting targets for companies and institutions to be more energy efficient, moving toward becoming carbon neutral. Wentworth Institute of Technology (WIT), in Boston, MA, USA, has a historically developed power system of supply, generation, and consumption. The purpose of this project was to investigate and document the currently existing electrical supply and demand on campus, and to explore possible expansion of renewable energy on campus. The supply for the existing system had an electrical input from the utility grid, a natural gas supplied cogeneration plant, and a small solar array on the roof of one building. The campus was supplied with 62 % of electricity from the utility grid, 38% from the cogeneration plant, and less than 1 % from the existing solar array. A goal was to explore whether more of the campus electrical demand could be supplied by renewable energy generated on the campus. For this study, a proposed new canopy solar array over an existing large parking lot, and another solar array on the roof of a gymnasium were explored. These additions would bring the amount of renewable energy generation on campus up to roughly 24 % of the demand, reducing the amount of energy supplied by the utility. This proposed system would reduce the carbon footprint of the campus and help move towards the carbon neutral targets.

articleTitle: Virtual SCARA Robot with Reduced Dynamics in a Real-Time Simulation Scheme for Robotics and Control Engineering Education
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Industry 4.0 has imposed new challenges and oppor-tunities to engineering education in robotics and control systems. The concept of the digital twin can be partially implemented with the use of virtual robots that incorporate 3D models and numerical simulations of the dynamical behaviour. This work presents the development of a virtual 3D SCARA robot which requires an external controller for the joint and kinematic motion control, this was implemented as a tool for teaching and learning robotics and control. The virtual 3D robot incorporates a novel numerical simulation that combines the Newton-Euler dynamic equations with the Rayleigh energy dissipation equation to consider the viscous friction. The developed virtual robot can be implemented in a real time simulation scheme connected to an external controller and used as an educational tool in a virtual robotics laboratory.

articleTitle: Optimal Mapping of DG Units in Island Partitioning Mode under Fault Condition Using BPSO: A Case Study of Thadi Feeder of Nepal
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The distribution system is one of the most crucial parts of a power system. In case of any emergency fault condition in the network, the islanding operation with available Distributed Generation (DG) will maintain the availability/ reliability of the system within acceptable limit. The available DGs must be allocated optimally such that maximum load will be restored in the system. The purpose of this study is to determine the best approach for restoring the post-fault distribution system. It utilizes the graphical algorithm to assign the load to the DGs and perform the load shedding problem using Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO), if there is any shortage of the power supply in the system. Also, the load flow analysis is also performed to check the feasibility of the obtained optimal mapping of DGs. This paper properly takes into account the load priorities factors, voltage limit, power imbalance issues and the line capacity requirements for the optimal operation of system. The methodology is applied to rural radial distribution network of Nepal Electricity Authority (NEA), Thadi feeder, Nepal. and the results reflects the optimal maximum restoration of the load during post fault conditions.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics in Healthcare: The Use of Machine Learning for Diagnoses
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Currently with COVID19 pandemic, health becomes an important factor in our daily life. There are many diseases, some are treatable, some are lethal. Predictive analytics is a method to predict an outcome based on historical data and has been used in many sectors including healthcare. In healthcare, all data are kept in an Electronic Health Record, and therefore can be used to predict healthcare issues including diseases. Machine Learning is a method can be used to select and train the data to make a decision. Different methods in machine learning have been used to predict diseases such as heart and lung diseases, cancer and many more. This paper discusses different methods such as Support Vector Machine, Neural Network with Decision Trees, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbor, and variations of those algorithms that have been used for prediction in the field of health and healthcare. The different methods are compared in terms of the accuracy. In conclusion, the accuracy of the predictions is acceptable, however some are still low. The challenges are to improve the accuracy using different machine learning algorithms or hybrid algorithms.

articleTitle: Trends in Web APIs Classification, Selection, and Composition
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The number of web services and web APIs is still growing. Due to that, the manual selection and possible manual composition of the services is difficult, which is why the research of automatic classification, selection and composition of the services is still actual. This paper reviews recent research on this topic, with the goal of defining the main topics and directions of future research. From the set of 80 read recent conference and journal articles, 30 most relevant papers were singled out. A review of the literature shows that the greatest potential lies in the topic of new services and web APIs (for example, Internet of Things services, machine and deep learning services and APIs) and approaches to classify, select and compose these types of services. The mentioned services have many specific features, and there are still no things, machine or deep learning as a services specific approaches in the existing literature.

articleTitle: Invention and Historical Development Efforts of Pinned Buried Photodiode
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper reviews the invention of Pinned Buried Photodiode in 1975 by Yoshiaki Hagiwara at Sony which is also called as Hole Accumulation Device (HAD) which was originally defined in the form of the P+NPNsub triple junction type dynamic photo thyristor structure with the in-pixel vertical overflow drain (VOD) function to realize the electric shutter function capability. The evidence of the invention is explained with the three Japanese Patent Applications applied by Hagiwara at Sony in 1975. The first double junction type Pinned Photodiode was also developed by Hagiwara Team at Sony in 1978 and reported in the Japanese domestic SSDM1978 conference in Tokyo. The three original Japanese Patent Applications, filed by Hagiwara in 1975, were the evidence of the invention, however, being written only in Japanese and unfortunately never having been applied in USP and other oversea patents. The details are now reviewed and disclosed here with the English translation of the original Japanese Patent Applications for the first time in the IEEE English speaking community. The triple junction type Pinned Buried Photodiode has inherently the image-lag-free feature, the in-pixel VOD function and the electric shutter function capability, that have completely replaced film media and mechanical parts from the modern high-definition solid-state digital cameras.

articleTitle: Grey Box Modelling of Supermarket Refrigeration Room
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Aiming to enable robust large-scale fault diagnostics and optimized control for supermarket refrigeration systems, a data-driven grey box model for cooling rooms and cabinets was developed. The analysis scopes a single cold room in a supermarket in Otterup (Denmark) and was done using one-minute of sampling data. A resistance-capacitor diagram of the room was analyzed to derive three state-space equations for the model - the following were the states: the room temperature, the temperature of the goods and the refrigerant mass in the evaporator. The model parameters were then estimated using a Kalman filter and the maximum likelihood method. In the present paper, the resulting model is demonstrated through a five-hour simulation and the importance of ongoing re-estimation of parameters is highlighted, as the dynamics of the room constantly change, as goods are added and removed. Furthermore, the physical meaning of the parameters is discussed and a case where the parameter estimates became physically meaningless is highlighted - suggesting that robustness was an issue and further studies with simpler models and other solver algorithms are necessary for large-scale implementation.

articleTitle: Application of data diodes in Internet of Things security
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The rapid growth of the ubiquitous connectivity of Internet of Things (IoT) devices causes major security challenges for these cyber connected things. Due to the lack of a standardised and universally accepted IoT implementation framework, conventional information technology (IT) security measures are applied to the heterogeneous stack of IoT technologies. However, IT security measures cannot always be directly applied to IoT security requirements. Thus, the transmission of data through the IoT network layer becomes inevitably vulnerable to attack. This paper proposes the application of data diodes to enhance the data security of the heterogeneous stack of IoT technologies. The paper also proposes the possibility of bringing IoT security to the edge (devices) by embedding miniature data diodes within IoT devices. Data diodes are hardware-based security measures that enforce only one way data flow. Thus, the devices have no physical reverse channels for incoming data from the outer network (Internet) by which most cyberattacks are carried out.

articleTitle: Global-Local Channel Attention for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) assigns a pixel-wise semantic label leveraging the rich information in the broad spectral band. However, most of the existent HSIC algorithm fail to take advantage of varying importance of different channels, which hinder the further improve of the performance. To this end, we originally propose a Global-Local Channel Attention (GLCA) module to assist the process of selecting useful channels while suppressing others. Working in a plug-and-play fashion, GLCA precisely re-calibrate channel-wise feature responses in a pixel-wise manner, flexible enough to be applied to any existing depth-based HSIC model with little additional computational cost. Rich experiments prove the effectiveness of our algorithm, and to the best of our knowledge, we establish new state-of-the-arts on multiple HSIC datasets.

articleTitle: Optimization of Battery Storage and Renewable Distributed Generations Allocation, Battery Charge-discharge Profile in Distribution Power Feeders
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The paper presents a study on the simultaneous determination of the optimal allocation of the battery storage system and renewable distributed generation units in power distribution systems using the co-simulation approach. A method for determining the optimal sizes/powers and locations of battery storage systems and distributed generation units based on a metaheuristic optimization technique is proposed. In addition to the optimal allocation, the optimal deployment of battery storage units is also considered and included in the optimization problem. The fuzzy based controller for battery storage charging/discharging is proposed and optimized simultaneously with allocation optimization. Minimization of system losses is considered as the objective of the optimization problem. The cosimulation approach is used to simulate the power system model and the optimization procedure. The presented optimization framework is applied to the IEEE 37 node test distribution feeder to present the procedure. The power losses are compared for three scenarios. The achieved reduction in power losses compared to the base case is 28.5 and 33.1 percent for scenarios 2–3, respectively.

articleTitle: Fourier-Bessel series neural networks for classification
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: An innovative neural network for classification where hidden neurons are built from double Fourier-Bessel series (FBSNN) is presented. Topology of neural network includes 2 inputs, single output and arbitrary number of hidden neurons. This FBSNN was tested for linearly separable and non-separable, 2- and 3-classes classification problems in machine learning techniques and applications. For comparison, the results obtained from FBSNN were also analyzed by the famous backward propagation neural networks (BP ANN) and radial basis function neural networks (RBFNN), simultaneously. The performance in training process and the decision boundaries of all testing cases are also compared and examined. We found that FBSNN can provides correct classification using small number of hidden neurons and offers very rapid convergence in training process as compared with BPANN and RBFNN.

articleTitle: Classification of Swallowing Foods Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: There are limits in assessing healthy and abnormal swallowing by Videofluoroscopic swallowing study. Classification of accelerometric swallowing signals is much more efficient method to judge healthy swallowing. However, these methods have developed mostly with dual axis accelerometric signals and classifying two-class problems. This study is to examine classification methods with multi-class three-axis accelerometric signals. Swallowing signals of five foods are classified with both supervised learning algorithm and unsupervised learning algorithm. Three-axis signals denoised by 10-level discrete wavelet transform with soft thresholding before feature calculation. The result confirmed that classification with support vector machine and K-nearest neighbor can predict with 90% accuracy. However, Classification with fuzzy c-mean clustering produce low purity and normalized mutual information.

articleTitle: Black Box Testing with Exploratory Approach of a Software for Remote Monitoring of Patients with COVID-19 and Other Infectious Diseases
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Covid-19 pandemic has set the world on fire. It has impacted every aspect of our society. One of the worst affected parts is the countries' health systems. Our goal is to provide a proof of concept for cost effective telemedicine system which can be used by hospitals for monitoring of thousands of patients at once, thus medical personnel exposure to the virus is minimized. In this paper we aim to put this system through the best practices of software testing so we can determine if it achieves its primary functions, keeping in line with the general idea of cost effectiveness. Black box testing with the exploratory approach was used for functionality and feature testing as it gives the most accurate real-world results. During the tests, several bugs were found and fixed. Because of the fact, that the testers were actual medical personnel, we have received valuable information on how to improve the quality of the product, so it can be even more ease to use and provide the necessary robustness and data visualization.

articleTitle: Positioning of multicapacitors in a radial distribution network using new analytical methods
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper consisted of sizing and positioning multiple capacitors at multi-node in the Maradi HV distribution network in Niger by a new modern analytical method based on the calculation of a stability identification index (BVSI). From this study, it is observed that the positioning of the 2100 kVAr, 1050kV Ar, and 2100 kV Ar power capacitors at node 31, node 84 and node 105 respectively in the 123-bus network of Maradi contributed to reducing the losses of this network by 20.71 % with a minimum voltage of 0.9172 pu. However, despite this improvement, 31.70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of the nodes still remained within the critical ranges, hence the need for other equipment to improve the performance of distribution networks. The traditional means of improving the technical performance of distribution networks by means of capacitors is nowadays insufficient to maintain the indicative parameters of the technical performance of distribution networks in emerging countries within the normative limits.

articleTitle: Simplified energy losses in power transformer calculations algorithm implemented in ION technology environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: An experiment was performed to calculate the power transformer losses due to current harmonics. During the experiment, a power meter with Modbus RTU communication and a programmable logic controller (PLC) were used. While testing the calculation algorithm, the influence of the reactive power compensation device on the power transformer losses due to the ongoing resonance was observed. In this work, the algorithm is transferred to a programmable power meter with an ION environment to achieve good sampling and integration frequency. The purpose of this work is to implement user friendly prototype for estimation of transformer losses due to current harmonics and low power factor in real time.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a CRLH Transmission Line Antenna of a Hilbert Fractal Geometry for S-Band Appications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: With the great developments of communication systems, the further needs for designing small-sized, high-gain antennas have been increased. Metamaterial made these challenges are possible to be realized. In this paper, a novel low-profile MTM unit cell was designed. The design structure is consistent of the symmetric CRLH unit cell, where a Hilbert-shaped structure compensates for via. The proposed antenna provides a significant enhancement over the original CRLH metamaterial unit cell. The antenna performances are evaluated in terms of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and gain using the CST MWS; the antenna is found to show a resonance frequency at 3.7 GHz with a gain equals to 3.08dBi and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>< -22dB. The proposed design has a low profile and small size make it very suitable for array applications.

articleTitle: Optimized management of Renewable Energy Sources in Smart Grids in a VPP context
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The increase in the world's population combined with the development of new economies has led to a large scale increase in the demand for energy resources. New technologies have emerged that allow for the maintenance of the energy supply. Renewable sources and energy storage systems (ESS) are emerging as a crucial option for the development of Smart Grids. Using a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) opti-mization model, the effects of renewable production sources and storage systems on an electrical grid were studied, in order to maximize the profit of a Virtual Power Plant (VPP). The obtained results allowed us to verify the efficiency of the proposed method. The placement of renewable producers and the ESS, as well as the management optimization of the purchase and transfer process of the stored energy definitely increased the profit of VPP. The use of these technologies also improves the voltage profile and decreased the active power losses by 84 % along with the network.

articleTitle: Determination of winding losses in magnetic integrated inductors and separate skin and proximity effects, magnetic and copper losses and study of evolution of the losses
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Losses within magnetic single layer inductors are represented by the dependent frequency resistance that is determined from simulated or measured scattering matrix parameters using admittance method described in [1]. In this method, losses are represented by the calculated or measured resistance RDC at low frequencies, by the resistance calculated from admittance Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> at medium frequencies, and by the resistance obtained at resonant frequency in high frequencies. Once calculated, losses origins will be identified and then separated in two parts: losses due to skin and proximity effects and magnetic and copper losses.

articleTitle: Audio Recording Device for Partial Discharge from Overhead Power Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Power system faults are disruptive and may lead to long power outages. One cause is the phenomenon of partial discharge (PD). PD events may result in damage to the insulation, junctions, and transmission lines. Early detection of PD events could be used to schedule preventative maintenance for the involved junctions and transmission lines. One approach to PD detection is by analyzing acoustic emissions near power lines to determine if a PD event has occurred. Due to interference and noise issues, methods to analyze audio emissions for identification of potential PD events need further development to become practical. The purpose of this project was to develop a prototype of an audio collection system with the ability to survive in an outdoor environment, record audio sounds, and transmit the recordings to external computers for storage, analysis, and identification of potential PD events. Such a device could be mounted outside near high-risk power lines and junctions for monitoring for potential PD occurrences. The use of such a device would contribute toward algorithm development to detect PD, which would assist scheduling of preventative maintenance.

articleTitle: Analysis and optimization of spectrum sharing in IMT-2020 and satellite systems considering harmful interferences
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The coexistence of IMT-2020 and satellite networks plays an important role in bridging the digital divide and for the economic and social development of rural areas and allows for extended coverage of mobile communications. In this context, for such a network defined as hybrid, adaptations and changes in transmission systems and media are essential to benefit from the advantages of coexistence. Many researches have been carried out, and through the literature, the technique of cognitive radio can be considered the most attractive. The objective of this paper is to study the problem of coexistence between the FSS system operating in the C-band and the IMT-2020 system in order to avoid harmful interference and to improve the spectrum efficiency (scarce resource). This work also presents two solutions to improve the network performance; the control of the transmit power of 5G antennas and the implementation of a reference filter at the ground stations. Probabilistic techniques such as Monte Carlo algorithm, root-raised-cosine filter (SRRC) model will be used to evaluate the impact of the 5G network cells on the satellite receivers. The results obtained show that in order to respect the interference threshold of the receivers, the minimum separation distance will have to be respected, and filters with a rejection value of more than 60dB will have to be equipped. The calculations and the simulation were made with the Matlab tool.

articleTitle: Implementation of Q-Learning Algorithm on Arduino: Application to Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation in COVID-19 Field Hospitals
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The recourse to Mobile Robots (MRs) in fighting against Coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) has today become a necessity in almost all hospitals worldwide. Indeed, for example, the Ultraviolet Disinfection (UVD) robot has been very useful, since COVID-19 pandemic began, to destroy viruses in Wuhan hospitals. However, MRs are equipped with a locomotion system, which should be capable of navigating through, generally, an unknown work environment. In such situation, MR should also have learning mechanism. In this paper, we propose a low-cost solution to deal with the problem of autonomous navigation and the trajectory optimization for MR in Field Hospitals (FHs). The architecture of these latter may be varying from one to another according to where it should be installed. Thus, a rapidly adapting to the new trajectory is then necessary to help save lives in pandemic situation. So, to conduct a successful autonomous navigation of MR particularly in COVID-19 FHs, a practical low-cost solution must then be found. To do so, a MR equipped with TCS230 Color Sensor, is used to read colored sticky notes fixed on the ground, to identify room number of the FH that serves for learning and correcting robot trajectory keypoints. Furthermore, an Android application is also developed in this work to remotely control, via a Bluetooth wireless connection, an Arduino-based MR in some specific situation. Some experiments were carried out to verify the performance of the proposed autonomous navigation approach of MR type ELEGOO Smart Robot Car V3.0. Moreover, the simulation results have confirmed that the robot can reach the goal with optimal trajectory by only exploiting the popular Q- Learning algorithm with the use of a low-cost color sensor, and sticky notes which could be easily deployed according to the architecture of the new installed FH.

articleTitle: Development of IoT Based Dust Density and Solar Panel Efficiency Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Solar energy is the most redundant substitute to declining non-renewable energy sources. However, numerous factors can reduce a solar panel's effectiveness. Accumulation of dust on solar panels has been proved as a major factor in reducing solar efficiency. However, the accumulation could differ significantly depending on time and location. This study investigates the accumulation of dust and efficiency of solar panel by developing an IoT based dust sensing system. An affordable IoT system was developed for the data collection. The system utilized easily available optical dust sensor and Wi-Fi enabled microcontroller The system used an IoT dashboard called, My Devices Cayenne to monitor the data collection from online. The data was collected for 1 month. This research utilized a research site and an open garage site for the location of data collection. Within one month, the accumulated amount of dust sensed by the sensor was 30411.53 mg/m3, and the solar panel's efficiency decreased from 15.42% to 0.74%. In the end, the efficiency reduction found in this study was compared with other similar studies where the efficiency loss of solar panel due to dust accumulation were also measured. In this study, the efficiency reduction was found to be around 15% whereas in other studies the efficiency reduction ranged from 11.8% to 21.5%

articleTitle: LADA: Locality Aware Distributed Addressing for Edge/Fog Computing Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In edge/fog computing infrastructures, the resources and services are offloaded to the edge and computations are distributed among different nodes instead of transmitting them to a centralized entity. Distributed Hash Table (DHT) systems provide a solution to organizing and distributing the computations and storage without involving a trusted third party. However, the physical locations of nodes are not considered during the creation of the overlay which causes some efficiency issues. In this paper, Locality aware Distributed Addressing (LADA) model is proposed that can be adopted in distributed infrastructures to create an overlay that considers the physical locations of participating nodes. LADA aims to address the efficiency issues during the store and lookup processes in DHT overlay. Additionally, it addresses the privacy issue in similar proposals and removes any possible set of fixed entities. Our studies showed that the proposed model is efficient, robust and is able to protect the privacy of the locations of the participating nodes.

articleTitle: A Charging Technique for Sensor Nodes in Wireless Rechargeable Sensor Networks for Cyber-physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Very recently, advances in wireless sensor networks have enabled wireless energy transfer and charging technology to efficiently deliver energy to depleted sensor nodes in a typical wireless rechargeable sensor network (WRSN) environment. With this current technology, the charging process is carried out by a wireless charging vehicle (WCV) which assist in charging each sensor nodes in the network. There is always a big possibility that most sensors will have their energies depleted while the WCV is serving other sensor nodes in the network. In this work, we develop an efficient scheme that aim to extend the lifetime of the WRSN. An inspection algorithm is developed to visit and inspect sensor nodes in the network so as to determine the set of sensor nodes to charge in order to aid the efficient use of the WCV. The simulation experiment carried out reveals that our proposed scheme performs better when compared to other schemes in terms of the survival rate of sensor nodes in the network.

articleTitle: Bayesian model calibration for bending stiffness assessment in OPGW cables
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In overhead transmission lines, due to wind action, OPGW cables can vibrate and oscillate as a result of different types of aerodynamic and aeroelastic instabilities. Therefore, studies to evaluate its dynamic behavior are necessary. This paper presents a Bayesian calibration model of a finite element model based on Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, intending to estimate the bending stiffness of the cable. For this purpose, experimental tests were performed in a laboratory span. The posteriors distributions of the bending stiffness and damping coefficient were obtained from the backward propagation of the experimental measurements. In addition, the uncertainty of the calibrated forward model was propagated and contrasted with the experimental data.

articleTitle: Fusion of Momentary Moods in Major Depression with Fuzzy Recurrence Analysis and Tensor Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Major depressive disorder has been modeled as a complex dynamical system. In this study, daily emotional changes in personalized depression were investigated using the concepts of fusion of recurrences and tensor decomposition. This study aims to answer the question if the use of the proposed approach can objectively discover what state of mind is considered as the most important attribute for differentiating the effect of medical alteration in major depression. By applying two different fusion models for combining time series of negative and positive moods obtained from a unique dataset of a case of personalized clinical depression, and the decomposition of these fusions by means of a multiway data analysis, the results suggest that while the interfusion of both negative and positive moods can be complementary, the intrafusion of negative moods would maximize the differenfiation.

articleTitle: Design of on-chip fractal antenna for wireless NoC
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Wireless communications in a network on a chip (N oC) have recently been proposed as a technology shift of existing wired interconnects to overcome their drawbacks such as latency and limited bandwidth. Performance analysis of a designed on chip antennas requires investigation of frequency channel link interference, which affects the N oC systems quality of service (QoS). In this context, this work proposes the design as well as the characterization of an antenna ensuring on chip wireless communication operating at millimeter waves (from 50 to 160 GHz). The antenna is multi-wide-bandwidth enabling high data rate links. Compared to state of the art, the proposed fractal antenna has a considerable bandwidth, gain and size which facilitate on-chip integration.

articleTitle: An Application of Command, Control, Computing, Communication, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Systems in the Protection of the Amazon Rainforest
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The limitations of the Amazon environment require technological developments to improved data acquisition and military systems for managing, processing and sharing information, ensuring to military operations greater flexibility, interoperability and helping the decision-making. This paper proposes a hardware-software architecture for Command, Control, Computing, Communication, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Systems (C4ISR) that is being designed within the scope of Brazilian Armed Forces. This architecture is based in an Unmanned Aerial Platform and comprises the technologies of (1) Command and Control Interoperability (INTERC2), an intelligent communication middleware; (2) Mission-Oriented Sensors Array (MOSA), which automates and optimizes data acquisition, data fusion and data sharing; (3) InFFlight Awareness Augmentation System (IFA2S), that provides security for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) navigation; (4) Data Mining techniques to work with data patterns; and (5) an adaptive system, composed by a Software Defined Radio (SDR) that promote the electromagnetic signals identification. This paper also presents a case study that describes the operational requirements for the application of a solution to increase the capability of defense of the Amazon rainforest using already existing infrastructures of the Brazilian defense monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Power Distribution System Failure and Vulnerability Analysis in Ethiopia
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper tries to study the causes of frequent distribution system failures and their effect for the vulnerability of the existing distribution components in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The study is a component-based failure analysis on a selected feeder of the Kotobie distribution system in Addis Ababa. The feeder is selected based on the frequency of interruptions. Feeder 6 of the substation is the most frequently interrupted line. The existing conditions of the distribution poles, conductors, insulators, transformers, protection devices, and other components on the feeder are inspected. The probable effect of the most frequent causes of interruption on the existing components of the selected feeder is studied. Sudden faults are usually due to weather influence. It accounts for 48.66% of the total known interruption causes, excluding interruptions due to operation. The weather and gravitational force influence on the existing tilted distribution poles is studied through COMSOL software. Considering the selected area weather condition, the decay depth of wooden poles is studied using TimberLife software. The effect of decay for failure is also simulated using COMSOL software. Poles could deflect 3.05° and 1.749° with and without considering decay depth at the worst condition of a single disturbance, respectively. The resilience condition is identified by analyzing deflection and stress on the surface of the poles. In addition, many of the existing distribution transformers are working overloaded. The loss of life of distribution transformers for their vulnerability is studied using the IEEE guide. 83 of 157 transformers are expected to lose their lives and sustain below the standard life, i.e., 20.55 years.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Clustering and Dynamic Feature Selection Methodology Based on Dimensional Isotropy Preservation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: There are some challenging issues in clustering problems and clustering methodologies, which frequently attract researchers’ interests. Ability of handling high dimensional feature space is among them, since robustness of all machine learning algorithms is reduced by the concept of “curse of dimensionality”. In unsupervised machine learning literature, a general consensus can be seen on the clustering process: If the data is high dimensional, as a preprocessing step, first reduce the number of dimension using dimension reduction techniques, then cluster data. However, such a kind of cascaded way may cause information loss and redundant repeating operations, consequently reduce the validity of the clustering output and may yield low quality clustering schema and bring more computational burden. In the literature there is no methodology, which is based on classical statistical concept and capable of handling high dimensional data, except graph theory based ones. In that study; a hybrid approach is proposed for high dimensional data clustering which is mainly based on subspace clustering and projected clustering using a statistical concept: isotropic position. More precisely, proposed algorithm deals with clustering by simultaneously feature selection upon dimensional isotropic preservation. As a result, preprocessing step for dimensional reduction will not be required, when proposed methodology is preferred for the clustering process. Moreover, since the principal features are selected dynamically in the proposed methodology by not a holistic concern of the dataset; high quality clustering schema is expected, while low computational burden will be incurred. Experimental analysis of the proposed algorithm points out promising results for simultaneous clustering and dimension reduction.

articleTitle: Definition of Performance Indicators for the “Human factor” Axis of a Graduate School's Balanced ScoreCard
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The decision information system (DIS), which has become a necessity for the performance of a company, has been developed in several areas. It is noted that solutions provided have their limits and are not adapted to all fields. This is the case of the research field. The lack of a DIS is generally noted at the level of graduate schools (GS). Moreover, studies on the working conditions of these GSs only consider PHD students and research professors. To overcome these limitations, a new decision support methodology (DSM) based on Balanced Scorecard (BSC) is needed. This paper aims to identify the indicators of the proposed new BSC axis for managing a GS overall performance. To achieve this, the results of surveys on the Definitive stakeholders of Senegalese GS, and the data taken at source, are studied. These indicators concern all the DSH. An adaptation of the BSC to the GS required the integration of a new axis called “Human factor” (Subjective, Intangible, and Behavior).

articleTitle: Foreword
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: It is our pleasure to welcome you to the IEEE International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET 2021) in Cape Town, South Africa. articleTitle: BRCLightning – Protection against atmospheric discharges on the palm of your hand
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This article presents the BRCLightning software developed as a database made available online and that can be accessed through various types of devices - desktops, laptops, tablets and smartphones. Therefore, it incorporates a responsive configuration to serve in an appropriate, objective, secure, safe, agile and easy way. The software has its interface organized as forms developed in the languages: Portuguese and English, which is defined in the login. This software was developed to meet the demands of engineers, design companies or those who need to manage Lightning Protection System - LPS - installed in their units, in addition to professionals qualified to develop design and diagnostics of these kinds of systems. It incorporates the requirements established in three Standards used in the conception of traditional lightning protection, which are: the Brazilian Association of Technical Standards-ABNT; International Electrotechnical Commission - IEC and the American National Fire Protection Association - NFPA. The architecture is composed of 4 Modules, whose functionalities are: the risk analysis to process the identification and quantify the risks arising from atmospheric discharges to the earth that can be dangerous to people, structures and power and signal lines established in the previously mentioned Standards; the sizing by the rolling spheres method and the angle methods, these two use the methodology of the mathematical approach developed by BRC engineering and one of the reports with groups of filters for issuing different report formats.

articleTitle: Managing Complex Interactions between Production and Failure Management: a System-theoretical Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper introduces and tests a system-theoretical model considering the complex interactions between operational production goals and reactive failure management. In particular, reactive failure management tasks are emphasized, including the analysis and correction of failures and their effects on production goals. For the determination of the proportionate influence of failure management on production, a system-theoretical model is developed. All production chains are represented by linking five modules (resources, production, defect introduction, root cause elimination and defect-based learning). This comprehensive modeling of modules enables the consideration of corresponding variables of production planning and control. A stock and flow diagram is used as an adequate means of description and visualization. Further, the formal model is converted into an executable simulation model. The verification and validation of the model are accomplished by reviewing specific aspects of all phase results. Tests performed on the final simulation model are described. Therefore, this paper improves the understanding of the complex relationship between production goals and handling failures and proves the importance of well-structured failure elimination processes.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Training System of PC Operation for Elderly, Using Gazing Point and Mouse Operation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this study, evaluation and training system for PC operation are proposed. In the proposed system, the gaze measurement device GP3 is used to measure the user's gazing point during PC operation without having a direct contact. The proposed system can also record the history of operating the mouse cursor position, clicks, etc., and understand the characteristics of the user's PC operation. The proposed system can perform two types of tasks: icon search task and mouse operation task, enabling users to understand and train their weaknesses. As an experiment to confirm the operation of the proposed system, the authors evaluated the PC operation ability of a healthy elderly female and a healthy adult male. As a result, the authors confirmed the possibility that the proposed system can provide feedback on the characteristics and operating ability in PC operation.

articleTitle: Neural Network based on Automatic Differentiation Transformation of Numeric Iterate-to-Fixedpoint
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This work proposes a Neural Network model that can control its depth using an iterate-to-fixed-point operator. The architecture starts with a standard layered Network but with added connections from current later to earlier layers, along with a gate to make them inactive under most circumstances. These “temporal wormhole” connections create a shortcut that allows the Neural Network to use the information available at deeper layers and re-do earlier computations with modulated inputs. End-to-end training is accomplished by using appropriate calculations for a numeric iterate-to-fixed-point operator. In a typical case, where the “wormhole” connections are inactive, this is inexpensive; but when they are active, the network takes a longer time to settle down, and the gradient calculation is also more laborious, with an effect similar to making the network deeper. In contrast to the existing skip-connection concept, this proposed technique enables information to flow up and down in the network. Furthermore, the flow of information follows a fashion that seems analogous to the afferent and efferent flow of information through layers of processing in the brain. We evaluate models that use this novel mechanism on different long-term dependency tasks. The results are competitive with other studies, showing that the proposed model con-tributes significantly to overcoming traditional deep learning models' vanishing gradient descent problem. At the same time, the training time is significantly reduced, as the “easy” input cases are processed more quickly than “difficult” ones.

articleTitle: Linear Prediction Matrix segmentation for Matrix Pencil Method in backscattering signal scenarios
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Here we propose and evaluate a method for segmenting the Linear Prediction Matrix used during the Matrix Pencil Method. This proposal considers the division of a time domain signal in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> frequency segments that can be processed individu-ally and whose results can be put together in the final stage. The evaluation of the suggested approach is presented here in terms of the coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R^{2}$</tex> for the reconstructed signal, and focuses on either reducing the hardware requirements for back-scattering signal processing, its parallelisation or reduced execution time for portable GPR operations.

articleTitle: A 1.6-GHz Low-Jitter, Low Reference-Spur Single-Loop Type-I PLL
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This work presents the design of a Low-Jitter Ring-VCO-Based single-loop type-I phase-locked loop (PLL) in 180 nm CMOS technology. To increase the phase detector (PD) gain and the margin phase of the PLL, a novel switched capacitor stage inside the Master-Slave Sampling loop filter is proposed. Furthermore, it allows reducing significantly the phase noise (PN) of the ring Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO). Also, a simple and less phase noise PD topology is discussed and compared to the typical XOR gate. From a 50-MHz reference input, a bandwidth of 25-MHz was obtained, leading to a simulated in-band PN of -118 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset, 486 fs of integrated jitter and spur level of -63 dB at 1.65 GHz for 10 mW of power consumption and 0.0099 mm 2 of core area.

articleTitle: Harvesting EM noise energy generated by the frequency power converter systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper describes the first experimental study of harvesting Electro-Magnetic (EM) noise energy resulted from the frequency power converter mechanism (called also frequency inverter) using bipolar antenna and conventional rectifier circuit. Our EM noise harvester based on commercial aluminum scotch ribbon and RB142 rectifier circuit was able to output 3 mA current and 10 Volts. The energy harvested reached 30 mW, which is more powerful than previous developed EM harvester. These results offer opportunities for self-powered electronic devices on a very large area of industrial applications.

articleTitle: The evaluation of Iranian government's role in the extension of wind energy: Technology penetration model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The urgent need for renewable energies in Iran confirms the importance of the government's support. In order to attain the government's support, the importance of designing new regulations' policy has dramatically increased. The main concern of this regulation policy is to reduce the cost of renewable energy equipment to become competitive with other conventional technologies. A critical factor in reducing the expenses is learning the impact of the functionality of renewable energies on increased economic output, which their impact is expressed in terms of technology learning rates. However, there are certain drawbacks associated with the government's support. A critical factor in reducing the expenses is learning the impact of the functionality of renewable energies on increased economic output, which their impact is expressed in terms of technology learning rates. However, there are certain drawbacks associated with the government's support. These supportive policies may not be permanent, which causes no economic justification for private investors to perform the whole process. In this paper, the cost-source curve of wind energy in Iran has been calculated to examine the efficiency of the protection policy. Moreover, the technology learning model, licensing model, and investor decision model are other influencing components in this study. The investor decision model is presented and categorized regarding the Rogers model. Investor recruitment is presented and categorized based on the Rogers model. The impact of long-term contract guarantee rates and administrative bureaucracy on the licensing process on investor behaviour is examined by this model. The results show that although the investors' primary concern should be the annual adjustment coefficient of the Purchase Guarantee Contract Rate, the administrative bureaucracy has hurt investor participation.

articleTitle: Social Network Analysis to Surveillance the Impact of Covid-19 in the African continent
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Pandemics originated by Covid-19 has caused many reactions in the world. Each country has reacted with different health policies. In this work, we analyze the publications of African citizens on Social networks (Twitter) to understand the pandemic scenario during the study period using a text mining approach. The study also adopted a statistical model to quantify the impact of daily COVID-19 cases on the frequency of tweets. Findings show that African tweets are related to awareness creation and policies to control the spread of COVID-19.

articleTitle: Detection of bacterial spot and yellow leaf curl virus in tomato leaves images using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: In this work, we propose an approach for automatic detection of bacterial spot and yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) in tomato leaves images. Our methodological is three steps: images pre-processing, images loading and classification. For this last step, we used convolutional neural networks with five (05) convolution layers coupled with dropout and batch normalization layers to avoid over-fitting the model. To train the model, we used two different datasets. The first one is the PlantVillage dataset containing 6927 color images of tomato leaves. The second dataset is made of 7087 images obtained by adding other images taken from other sources to those of PlantVillage. With both datasets, our model has an accuracy of about 98% during training phase. Nevertheless, when used with 72 images of tomato leaves taken in a real environment, the model trained with the dataset obtained by adding images from other sources to those from PlantVillage gives the best accuracy rates. It gave respectively 92%, 88% and 46% as true detection rate of bacterial spot, TYLCV and healthy leaves, while model trained with PlantVillage gave respectively 27%, 94 % and 0%.

articleTitle: Comparing recent Swarm Algorithms with Information Theoretic Filter criterion for Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Feature selection is getting significant importance in the fields of machine learning specially for dealing with high dimensional datasets. Feature selection techniques such as swarm algorithms have proven to be very effective in extracting meaningful information from large amounts of high dimensional data, thus improving prediction performance and reducing computation time. In this research, we evaluate the effectiveness of introducing mRMR (minimum Redundancy-Maximum Rel-evance) as an information theoretic filtering criterion on top of swarm optimization algorithms to further improve on existing techniques. We also present a comparison of the performances of two recent swarm algorithms against the well-known Artificial Bee Colony algorithm after incorporating mRMR-based filtering to demonstrate the applicability of this technique.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of the variable step-size Griffiths' LMS algorithm for fetal electrocardiography
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of the variable step-size Griffiths” LMS (VGLMS) algorithm for the separation of the fetal electrocardiogram (FECG) from the maternal electrocardiogram (MECG). The VGLMS algorithm is known for its observation noise free step size and gradient and hence its efficiency is explored for the purpose of fetal electrocardiography. Its performance is analyzed and compared with that of the normalized least mean squares (NLMS) algorithm. The comparison of these adaptive algorithms is carried out by choosing optimal filter lengths and step sizes which are chosen in order to maximize the signal to noise ratios (SNR) of the filtered signals. The SNR achieved by the algorithm, the power spectral density (PSD) and the weight vector convergence are chosen as the parameters of comparison. The superiority of the VGLMS algorithm over the NLMS algorithm is witnessed. The average SNRs achieved were 4.129dB and 0.922dB by the VGLMS and NLMS algorithms respectively.

articleTitle: Synthesis, Characterization, and Analysis of NaCaZn2Br6 for solar Cell Application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Perovskites are at the forefront of research into possible replacements for cumbersome and expensive silicon based solar cells. Lead based inorganic and organic-inorganic hybrid perovskite solar cells have been breaking records for efficiency, approaching 25 percent in recent years. However, these suffer from instability problems along with the possible health hazards in the long term. Hence, there has been a parallel search for lead-free, and preferably inorganic, perovskite solar cells in the hope of matching and ultimately exceeding the achievements of lead perovskite analogues. In this study, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NaCaZn2Br6$</tex> was synthesized using solution and solid state methods. The optical characterization was carried out using Ultraviolet-Visible (UV-VIS) spectroscopy. The electronic characterization was performed using SCAPS-1D to obtain Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE), doping density, flat band potential, and external quantum efficiency (QE). The solar cell structure used was ZnO/TiO2/NaCaZn2Br6/P3HT. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NaCaZn2Br6$</tex> was found to have a band gap of 3.85 electron volts, and the NaCaZn2Br6-based perovskite solar cell had efficiencies of 1.43 percent, 1.53 percent, 1.53 percent, and 1.91 percent at perovskite thicknesses 100, 10, 1, and 10 nanometers respectively. NaCaZn2Br6 is also found to be a p-type semiconductor based on the positive flat band potential. The external quantum efficiencies indicate higher instability at the higher thicknesses. It is recommended that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$NaCaZn2Br6$</tex> be synthesized using different synthetic routes and modified with dopants in order to increase its stability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Four-Channel Microstrip based RF Switchable Filter for S-band Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Nowadays, electronic countermeasure (ECM) devices are widely used to mislead early warning radars. In an ECM system, an RF filter is a vital component to define the band of operation. In this work, a four-channel switchable bandpass filter (BPF) in S-band with low insertion loss, promising isolation, and high-power handling capability is presented. For this, a microstrip-based open-loop ring resonator is designed to collect the jamming signals, coming from the foe, need to be identified and intercepted adequately. The proposed switchable BPF is having frequencies 2.2, 2.4, 2.6, and 2.8 GHz. A T-shaped combiner is also designed to act as a frequency combiner. At each channel, reasonable bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 140$</tex> MHz with an insertion loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) < 2.0 dB is achieved, while the isolations among the channels are better than 33 dB.

articleTitle: Visualizations of Third-Party Applications on DCS Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: The article presents a possible approach to integrating external applications with Distributed Control Systems (DCS). In the case under study, two different mechanisms of integrating the operator's decision support system were used. The main emphasis was placed on the practical aspects of solutions based on C # .Net and Python programming languages. The applied approaches guarantee flexibility of use, thanks to which it is easier to adjust the production solution to the existing infrastructure and internal policies in production plants. Moreover, this universal approach indicates the possibility of using various operating systems as a base platform for embedding systems based on Artificial Intelligence (AI). An additional advantage of the described approach is the ease of integration with various types of advanced data analysis tools, based both on an unconventional approach (e.g. Business Intelligence Tools) and non-standard solutions.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Low-Power Intrusion Detection System for IoT
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Technological advances in internet of things have enabled processing, storage and retrieval of information with minimal resource overhead. However, these battery-powered systems cannot host computationally intensive intrusion detection and prevention systems such as cloud-based machine learning intrusion detectors or blockchain encryption. We propose a low-power security setup for the internet of things. Power consumption is reduced by under clocking the gateway device processor, limiting peripherals and employing efficient network intrusion detection schemes. Security performance of the system is validated by comparing penetration test results for the power-optimized system and a baseline system running on default power configurations. This setup confirms that power savings of up to forty four percent can be achieved without compromising system security.

articleTitle: Heuristic Evaluation for Five Governmental Websites in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Government communicates with citizens through different channels. One of the most common channels is websites. There is no doubt that this communication is affected by the usability of those websites. Citizens would probably become confused or frustrated when a website lacks some core principles of usability. Thus, this study aimed to identify the usability problems of government websites. Specifically, it examined five governmental websites in Saudi Arabia by using heuristic evaluation. Eight evaluators assessed the five websites in terms of certain heuristics: navigation, interactivity, consistency, screen appearance, media use, and content management. The results showed that all five governmental websites had several types of usability issues. The recommendation of this study describes the importance of using modes (such as night reading and color blindness) and avoiding parallel translating for all pages.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ride through Method to Enhance DC-link Voltage Stability in Grid-Connected Doubly Fed Induction Generator Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Wind energy systems operating with a fixed DC-link voltage throughout voltage sag can cause power fluctuations and an increased current total harmonic distortion. This work proposes an adaptive approach to control DC-link voltage, enhance Low Voltage Ride-Through (L VRT) and system stability. In the proposed approach, the reference voltage value of the DC-link is computed from grid voltage and the voltage drop in the filter by an algorithm that checks any variation between the filter reference current and the minimum reference current. With the proposed method, when voltage sag happens the current distortions and the fluctuating voltages are drastically reduced and the transient response is improved. Fast reactive power injection has been performed and the protection (crowbar) activation can be avoided for a voltage drop up to 50% of deep. The proposed method is validated through detailed simulation in Matlab-Simulink.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Framework for Priority-Based Service Provisioning in Cloud
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Cloud computing provides the infrastructure for posting a variety of computing applications on the back-end servers. The hosted applications may have different priorities of execution and to the satisfaction of cloud users, their applications must be executed as per their priorities. Cloud computing is inherently susceptible to failures which often result in unreliable and delayed application execution. This paper proposes a framework for priority-based fault tolerant computing service in cloud. Users' applications are characterized as CRITICAL, PREMIUIM and NORMAL in the order of their priority, with CRITICAL applications of highest priority and NORMAL applications of lowest priority. The Cooperative Computing System (CCS) proposed for grid computing is further customized in this paper for cloud computing. The customized framework is evaluated through extensive simulation experiments by executing a set of 5000 applications of mixed priorities by varying the applications' duration and resource failure rate. The promising results obtained in terms of execution delay, service reliability and system throughput for the applications of different priorities justify the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Investigation of the properties of the model of a branched power supply network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Electricity supply networks ensure the joint operation of various types of energy sources, energy storage facilities and regulate the distribution of energy between consumers. To implement them, it is necessary to investigate their properties and form models. Modeling power grids allows you to achieve optimal operating parameters and understand their dependencies. In this paper, a minimum spanning tree with a fixed number of consumers is used to model a distributed network. A number of examples of networks with a similar structure are considered. The model was used to analyze the relative position of the branches and vertices of the spanning tree. Locations of chains of locally dependent vertices are determined. The impedance of the extended network was analyzed and the impedance of the model was calculated. An assessment of the application of the ladder formula to the calculation of the impedance of the model is given.

articleTitle: State of Art Approaches for Giving Related Items in Search Query
publicationTitle: 2021 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Energy Technologies (ICECET)
abstract: Search queries are used to dig out needed information and are one of the most important factors in assessment of search engines results. Search queries are consisting of words, phrases and keywords etc. Related items in the form of different appropriate words that can be used in search query to enhance its precision. Enhancement is done in many ways like suggesting correct spelling of misspelled words, autocomplete etc. To be more precise search queries are précised commonly by query replacement and query enhancement using query substitution and expansion approaches. In this paper we have categorized query precising approaches according to type of query. Query types are classified as transactional, navigational and informational. The paper analyses the pros/con of approaches along with challenges that needs to be addressed which will result in accurate query which eventually helps to get precise search results.

articleTitle: A New Approach for Long Term Electricity Load Forecasting for Uttarakhand State Power Utilities using Artificial Neural Network
